title: With Due Respect (Vol. 7) -- Ch. 15: Visionary Leadership by Example
keywords: CJP's debut as an Inquirer columnist
primary_topics: Chapter 15 of 'With Due Respect' (Vol. 7) -- CJP's February 11, 2007 Inquirer column, his very first, opening with his own journey 'from hawking newspapers in the backstreets of Sampaloc... to becoming the president of the most widely read newspaper'

His keynote to the Ayala Young Leaders Congress (AYLC) on the necessity of a clear 'vision-mission' -- 'specific and quantifiable,' value-laden and time-bound -- likened to a pilot announcing a destination and route

His illustrations of organizations driven by vision (the Inquirer and GMA Network) and the George Patton maxim that wars 'are won by soldiers' -- by 'the spirit of the men who follow and of the man who leads'

His thesis that, beyond vision, 'leading by example is the best, if not the only, way' -- shown by Manuel V. Pangilinan's first three days at PLDT (selling surplus cars, banking commissions, arriving at 8 a.m.), after which PLDT's worth 'multiplied tenfold' and 'its corporate ethics, a hundredfold'
sub_topics: The personal frame: 'one of the ringing joys' of CJP's life is his journey 'from hawking newspapers in the backstreets of Sampaloc, Manila to becoming the president of the most widely read newspaper' -- and, after 'more than 11 years on the Supreme Court,' his return to the Inquirer 'as a column writer'

AYLC 2007: the Ayala Corporation's annual gathering of '75 of the country's most outstanding student leaders' -- that year (Feb. 7-9, Tagaytay) on the theme 'Leading in Challenging Times,' attended by the Zobels -- where CJP keynoted that 'every leader and every organization... must have a clear idea of what they ultimately want to accomplish'

The vision-mission: as a journey needs 'a pre-selected destination, and a specific mode of how to get there' (like a pilot announcing the route), so 'must every leader have a vision-mission' -- one that is 'specific and quantifiable, not a mere collection of motherhood principles,' includes 'core values' and is 'achievable within a declared period'

The leader's role: by committing to 'goals, values, methods, and timetables,' the leader gives 'followers... general directions,' his role being 'to inspire and motivate the followers... to excel beyond themselves, and to achieve collectively their loftiest dreams'

The Patton maxim: quoting George Patton that wars 'are won by soldiers' -- by 'the spirit of the men who follow and of the man who leads' -- CJP applies it 'not only in the military... but in all human endeavors'

Vision in practice: the Inquirer leads as 'the largest circulated daily' because of its clear vision (to be 'the dominant, most respected and influential Philippine media organization') and 'mission' (a 'world-class processor of news and information') anchored on core values; GMA Network's vision likewise places 'God above all' -- both pursued 'doggedly... into fruition' by leaders Marixi Prieto and Felipe Gozon (CJP himself later joining GMA7)

Leading by example: a new chief executive of 'a huge Philippine company,' finding 'more than five dozen' cars assigned to his office, 'retained only one' and sold the rest; on day two he 'ordered' a briefcase of commission cash 'deposit[ed]... in the company's bank account'; and on day three, finding executives arriving 'about 10:00 a.m.,' he quietly arranged to be 'at office 8 a.m. daily'

The PLDT lesson and the thesis: that executive was Manuel V. Pangilinan, who in three days led 'in practising the prudent use of corporate assets, integrity in money matters, and on-time office arrival' -- after which PLDT's 'market worth... multiplied tenfold, and its corporate ethics, a hundredfold'; for though there are 'many ways to lead,' and charisma or media or genes 'have propelled many people to center stage,' 'leading by example is the best, if not the only, way to accomplish the vision/mission' -- by which the Inquirer, GMA7 and PLDT 'climbed to the top,' as 'can any organization,' and perhaps 'the Philippines'

one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 15 of 'With Due Respect' (Vol. 7), CJP's February 11, 2007 Inquirer column -- his very first, and the volume's closing piece -- opens with 'one of the ringing joys' of his life: the journey 'from hawking newspapers in the backstreets of Sampaloc... to becoming the president of the most widely read newspaper,' and now, after 'more than 11 years on the Supreme Court,' his return to the Inquirer 'as a column writer.' Keynoting the Ayala Young Leaders Congress (75 student leaders, on 'Leading in Challenging Times'), he argued that 'every leader and every organization... must have a clear idea of what they ultimately want to accomplish': as a journey needs 'a pre-selected destination, and a specific mode of how to get there' (like a pilot's announced route), 'so must every leader have a vision-mission' -- one 'specific and quantifiable, not a mere collection of motherhood principles,' value-laden and 'achievable within a declared period.' Quoting George Patton that wars 'are won by soldiers' -- by 'the spirit of the men who follow and of the man who leads' -- he points to the Inquirer (the largest daily, on a clear vision to be 'the dominant, most respected and influential' media organization) and GMA Network (whose values place 'God above all'), pursued 'doggedly... into fruition' by Marixi Prieto and Felipe Gozon. But beyond vision, he insists, 'leading by example is the best, if not the only, way': a new CEO of 'a huge Philippine company,' finding 'more than five dozen' cars assigned to his office, kept one and sold the rest; banked a briefcase of commission cash; and quietly began arriving at '8 a.m.' That CEO was Manuel V. Pangilinan, whose three days of modeling 'prudent use of corporate assets, integrity in money matters, and on-time office arrival' multiplied PLDT's worth 'tenfold' and 'its corporate ethics, a hundredfold' -- proof that 'using visionary leadership by example, the Inquirer, GMA7, and PLDT climbed to the top,' as 'can any organization,' and perhaps 'the Philippines.'
